Adding Emphasis
You add emphasis in a sentence by stressing important words or by adding words to support your intention. You add different words to emphasize different thing or situations.
You add time phrases like whenever, day in, day out, or over and over to highlight the time of an action.
You add do to emphasize a verb action.
You add ... at all to emphasize a negative attribute of an adjective or phrase.
Remember, when you stress a word, your intonation rises and the word is said slightly longer and louder than the other words.

Heteronyms
Heteronyms are words that have the same spelling but have a different pronunciation. Usually, heteronyms represent the different way of pronouncing the same word in two different forms of speech.
In many cases, the same word can be used as a noun and as a verb in English. The way you pronounce nouns and verbs follows a similar pattern.
For two syllable words, the noun is stressed on the first syllable, and the verb is stressed on the second syllable.

Example:
subject (noun)
subject (verb)

images.text: Where in the URL have I been on the computer? Ads have been chasing me all week! Whenever I go online, there they are doggedly following me!  I alternate browsers hoping for an alternate experience, but the ad hounds have my scent! They pop up at me over and over again!

Last year I looked up incontinence products for my grandmother. After that, there they were, to the left, to the right at the top and at the bottom of every single page I visited! Advertisers on the net appropriate spaces on every page - not appropriate at all! They have made their entrance, hoping to entrance me, hoping I will purchase perchance?
I attribute some of this to my least positive attribute, laziness. I am not content to jettison the content from my browsing data. That way I'd have to record all those names to have a record of my favorite places, then separate them all into separate groups. I do remember the last time I deleted those URLs, something I should not have done on my own, I lost every password.

Then I had to resign to resigning in at every website I frequent. Then, after that, I had to subject myself to studying up on the subject of erasing my digital imprint while keeping the things that I wanted. My frequent wanderings on the net are better now, for the most part anyway. I will purge the download data, cookies, cached images and files and browsing history, and then start again fresh in the morning.
